extraction.name: CoNLL-2003 Named Entity Recognition Dataset
extraction.description: A dataset for language-independent named entity recognition covering English and German, with annotations for four types of named entities: persons, locations, organizations, and miscellaneous entities. The English data was taken from the Reuters Corpus and the dataset includes training, development, test, and unannotated data files for each language.
extraction.creator: Erik F. Tjong Kim Sang and Fien De Meulder
extraction.rai:dataCollection: English data was taken from the Reuters Corpus (news stories between August 1996 and August 1997). German data was taken from the ECI Multilingual Text Corpus, specifically from the German newspaper Frankfurter Rundschau. Named entity tagging of training, development, and test data was done by hand at the University of Antwerp, mostly following MUC conventions.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Reuters Corpus news stories (English) and ECI Multilingual Text Corpus excerpts from Frankfurter Rundschau newspaper (German). The unannotated data contain 17 million tokens (English) and 14 million tokens (German).
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: English: training/development from end of August 1996, test set from December 1996, raw data from September 1996. German: training/development/test from one week at end of August 1992, raw data from September to December 1992.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Named entity tagging was done by hand at the University of Antwerp, mostly following MUC conventions. An extra named entity category called MISC was added to denote all names not in other categories.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: MBT tagger used for English POS tagging and chunking; Treetagger used for German lemmatization, tagging, and chunking. These were preprocessing tools, not NE annotation tools.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Tokenization, part-of-speech tagging, and chunking were applied to raw data. English data was tagged and chunked by the memory-based MBT tagger. German data was lemmatized, tagged and chunked by the decision tree tagger Treetagger. Named entity tagging of training, development, and test data was done by hand at the University of Antwerp following MUC conventions, with an extra MISC category added.

name.evidence: We describe the CoNLL-2003 shared task: language-independent named entity recognition. We give background information on the data sets (English and German)

description.evidence: The CoNLL-2003 named entity data consists of eight files covering two languages: English and German. For each of the languages there is a training file, a development file, a test file and a large file with unannotated data.

url.evidence: Data files (except the words) can be found on http://lcg-www.uia.ac.be/conll2003/ner/

creator.evidence: Erik F. Tjong Kim Sang and Fien De Meulder, CNTS - Language Technology Group, University of Antwerp

publisher.evidence: We describe the CoNLL-2003 shared task: language-independent named entity recognition.

inLanguage.evidence: The participants of the 2003 shared task have been offered training and test data for two other European languages: English and German.

rai:dataCollectionTimeframe.evidence: between August 1996 and August 1997. For the training and development set, ten days' worth of data were taken from the files representing the end of August 1996. All three of the training, development and test sets were taken from articles written in one week at the end of August 1992. The raw data were taken from the months of September to December 1992.
